column2: Israel again does evil before the Lord; the selected short opening has no added Ehud death notice.
The Lord sells Israel to Jabin of Canaan at Hazor, and Sisera commands his force from Arisoth of the Nations; the two officials and locations remain distinct.
Nine hundred iron chariots and twenty years of mighty oppression explain Israel's cry; the figures and chariot material remain explicit.
column3: The he/his reference belongs to the enemy power in context, with Sisera and Jabin both preceding; no new explicit subject is supplied.

column2: Deborah is prophetess, wife of Lappidoth and Israel's judge at that time; the selected feminine roles remain explicit.
Her palm stands between Ramah and Bethel in Ephraim's hill country, and Israel comes there for judgment; the purpose of their ascent remains.
Deborah summons Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, recalling the Lord's command involving Tabor and ten thousand from Naphtali and Zebulun.
column3: The inherited quotation makes the command direct speech and closes the question after 4:7; the publisher punctuates a question at the end of 4:6. Both units' clauses remain, but the speech punctuation is editorial.

column2: The first-person promise draws Sisera, his chariots and multitude to Barak at Kishon and gives him into Barak's hand; the divine speaker is inferred from the command context.
Barak's paired conditions for going and not going remain, followed by his ignorance of the day the Lord prospers the messenger with him; the longer messenger clause is preserved.
column3: The identity and attachment of the messenger with me remain open; ordinary human address to Deborah does not resolve messenger theology.

column2: Deborah's emphatic promise to accompany, warning about Barak's advantage and sale of Sisera into a woman's hands remain before the journey to Kedesh.
column3: Advantage is a working rendering of proterēma; the military precedence/honor nuance needs lexical assessment rather than automatic substitution of glory.

column2: Barak summons Zebulun and Naphtali, ten thousand ascend at his feet, and Deborah joins; the feet image is retained.
The selected neighbours of the Kenite separate from Jobab's sons, then an unnamed singular man pitches his tent by the Oak of the Resters near Kedesh.
column3: The plural neighbours and singular tent-pitcher remain unresolved; Jobab's gambros relation is left as in-law, and Heber is not inserted into this unit.

column2: An unnamed plural party reports Barak's ascent of Tabor to Sisera; no invented messenger group is named.
All Sisera's chariots, explicitly nine hundred iron ones, and all his people travel from Arisoth of the Nations to Kishon; the parenthetical figure is retained in dashes.
Arise, the appointed day, completed divine giving and the Behold question precede Barak's descent with ten thousand; the question remains rather than becoming a bare assertion.
The Lord confounds Sisera, all chariots and all camp before Barak, while Sisera dismounts and flees on foot; agency and the sword-edge phrase remain.
Pursuit reaches the Woodland of the Nations, and none of Sisera's camp remains; the translated woodland expression is not silently normalized to the earlier Arisoth form.
Sisera's flight reaches Jael, Heber the Kenite's wife, because of peace between Jabin and Heber's house; both family and political relations remain.
Jael's repeated turn-aside invitation, my lord, reassurance and hide covering remain; lord is ordinary human address and lowercase.
Sisera asks for a little water because of thirst; Jael opens a milk skin, gives a drink and covers his face, preserving the selected body-part detail.
The door instruction, conditional visitor question and commanded No remain, followed by the repeated hide covering; the final covering is not removed as redundant.
Jael takes the peg and mallet, approaches quietly and drives through the jaw to the ground; convulsing between her knees, breathing last and dying all remain.

Keep initial Behold and the final there lay as the second discovery marker. Replace entered with her with went in to her for eisēlthen pros autēn; the selected preposition does not explicitly state accompaniment. The jaw and peg remain.
The Lord God subdues Jabin of Canaan before Israel that day; the fuller divine title and named human object remain.
Israel's hand grows stronger and stronger against Jabin until his destruction; the repeated progression of the Greek is represented without changing the endpoint.
Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sing and speak that day; English plural agreement accommodates the compound subjects, while this introductory unit remains prose.
Leaders beginning to lead and the people's willing choice lead to the blessing command; the verbal leadership repetition remains. Proposed line breaks follow the two circumstances and exhortation.
Kings and mighty satraps are called to hear, then the singer promises song to the Lord and music to Israel's God; three clauses receive separate lines.

Direct singular address to the Lord retains Thou didst twice, Seir and Edom, shaken earth, astonished heaven and water-dropping clouds; the two departure clauses and cosmic responses receive line breaks.
Shaken mountains, this Sinai and repeated before the Lord remain; the compact dash-linked wording is retained without adding spaces or changing its normalized text.
column3: The syntactic relation of this Sinai to mountains is compressed; no alternate melting image is supplied.

column2: Shamgar and Jael frame the cessation of kings and repeated travel on paths and twisted roads; kings is the selected reading, not highways.
Phrazōn and repeated ceased remain, followed by third-person Deborah arose and a mother arose; the poem is not shifted to first-person I arose.
column3: Phrazōn is opaque and remains transliterated; the inherited lexical question is carried forward rather than replaced with village life or warriors.

column2: New gods, barley bread, a covering of lances and forty thousand remain in the inherited difficult comparison and question.
column3: The conditional ean idō construction, barley-bread relation and covering/lance phrase require specialist review; inherited question punctuation is provisional, not a settled parsing.

column2: My heart concerns the appointed things for Israel, followed by mighty people blessing the Lord; the neuter appointed things is not replaced by leaders.
Riders of beasts of burden and sitters in covered carriages remain as addresses continued into the command at 5:11; no added white animal description is supplied.
column3: Lampēnai is provisionally rendered covered carriages; vehicle terminology needs lexical confirmation.

column2: The command to utter musicians' sound among rejoicers, future ascription of righteousness, righteous people's strength and descent to His cities remain as four clauses.
column3: The participial musicians expression and the possessor of his cities remain interpretive; capitalization treats the Lord as antecedent provisionally.

column2: All four awake imperatives, rousing myriads, song, Barak's rising, Deborah's strengthening of Barak and captivity command remain; lineation follows the successive calls without deleting repetition.
The question about his magnified strength precedes a direct appeal to the Lord to humble stronger opponents for me; there is no second-person pronoun requiring Thou in this unit.
column3: The antecedent of his in the opening question remains unspecified.

column2: Ephraim's punishment, Benjamin's valley, your peoples, from me Machir, investigators, the Lord fighting and the sceptre/leadership phrase remain without reconstruction.
column3: Speakers, your brother/your peoples, the attachment of Machir and the final sceptre construction are unresolved. Ordinary your does not silently identify the addressee as God after 5:13's prayer.

column2: Issachar with Deborah, his foot soldiers, the question about dwelling between lips, stretching at his feet and Reuben's heart scrutiny remain distinct clauses.
column3: The he/his antecedents, lips expression and object of stretched out are uncertain; no familiar Barak or sheepfold wording is imported.

column2: Sitting for me between mosphathaim, hearing those rousing whistle and crossing into Reuben's territory retain the selected wording before heart searchings.
column3: Mosphathaim and the syntax connecting crossing with the final nominal clause remain opaque; they are not replaced by a reconstructed shepherd scene.

column2: Gilead beyond Jordan, Dan with ships and Asher at seashore/breaches remain; the question targets Dan and the first and last descriptions remain statements.
column3: Breaches for diakopai is provisional; harbors or inlets would require geographical/lexical justification.

column2: Zebulun scorns its life to death, with Naphtali on the field heights; the selected difficult verb is retained without converting the image into a generic bravery statement.
Kings arrive and array, Canaan's kings fight by Taanach/Megiddo water, and no greedy silver gain is taken; the final negative is retained.
Stars fight from heaven and their appointed order against Sisera; repetition of fought remains and meta is interpreted adversatively with the fighting verb.
Kishon, the repeated torrent and Kadēmim remain, followed by the future action of my mighty soul. The dash-connected torrent phrase stays intact; the final action receives its own line.
column3: Kadēmim and the referents of them remain unresolved; no ancient-torrent or imperative soul wording is substituted.

column2: The horse's heels are cut off, followed by Amadarōth of his mighty ones; the selected passive cutting image remains.
column3: Amadarōth and its possessive reference are opaque; no galloping-hooves reconstruction is claimed.

column2: The messenger's curse on Meroz, intensified curse on inhabitants, failure to help the Lord and the Lord as our mighty helper remain; the final statement is not omitted or made a human-warrior subject.
Jael, Heber the Kenite's wife, receives two wishes for blessing among women, the second in a tent; the optative sense is maintained with be/may.
Water requested becomes milk given, and butter arrives in a mighty-ones bowl; the contrast and concrete food terms remain.
column3: Butter for boutyron is provisional historical food terminology; curds is an alternative requiring contextual lexical assessment.

column2: Left hand toward a peg, right toward cuttings of the exhausted, cutting down Sisera, crushing the head and shattering/piercing the jaw remain; no familiar hammer clause replaces the selected right-hand wording.
column3: Apotomas katakopōn is an inherited unresolved lexical/syntactic problem; the working English exposes rather than resolves it. Cutting down may also require refinement after specialist review.

column2: The repeated between her feet, bending, falling and lying remain, ending wretched; line breaks retain the repeated locations and collapse no action.
Sisera's mother looks through window and lattice toward returning companions, then asks two questions about his delayed chariot and tracks; no wailing verb absent here is supplied.
Her wise noble ladies answer and she answers in her own words; both responses remain before the next unit's speech.
The question about finding him dividing spoil, befriending friends, head of a mighty man and repeated dyed/embroidered spoil remain, including his neck.
column3: The friends clause and its grammatical attachment are unresolved; no women-captive wording from another textual form is imported. Inherited punctuation is provisional.

column2: Thine preserves direct singular address to the Lord, followed by third-person those who love Him and the sun image; the forty-year rest closes as narrative, separated by an extra line break.
column3: The shift from Thine to Him is selected and retained; capitalization identifies the latter with the Lord provisionally rather than changing it to Thee.
